beginner.summary: For developers, data engineers and ML engineers who can write Python and understand what an embedding is, but have not used Milvus. Covers the Milvus deployment modes (Lite, Standalone, Distributed and Zilliz Cloud), the pymilvus MilvusClient API, collection schemas and field types, embeddings with pymilvus.model, insert, upsert and delete, AUTOINDEX and metric types, loading and searching collections, scalar, JSON and ARRAY filter expressions, query and count, partitions, Attu, the WebUI and the RESTful API v2, ending with a semantic document search capstone on Milvus Standalone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3.10+ scripts with virtual environments, pip and basic list and dict handling
Understands at a conceptual level what an embedding vector is and why similar items have nearby vectors
Has a Linux or macOS machine (or WSL2 on Windows) with Docker and Docker Compose, at least 8 GB RAM and rights to install Python packages
outcomes: Choose between Milvus Lite, Standalone, Distributed and Zilliz Cloud for a given workload and connect to each with MilvusClient
Design collection schemas with primary keys, scalar, JSON, ARRAY and vector fields, then insert, upsert and delete entities
Index, load and search collections with the right metric type and combine vector search with scalar, JSON and ARRAY filters
Operate a Docker-based Milvus Standalone instance and inspect it with Attu, the WebUI and the RESTful API v2

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already build collections, insert data and run filtered searches in Milvus and now need to tune and extend them. Covers HNSW, IVF and quantized index tuning with recall measurement, scalar indexes, partition keys and multi-tenancy strategies, consistency levels, BM25 full-text search with analyzers, text_match, hybrid dense and sparse search with RRF and weighted rankers, BGE-M3, range and grouping search, iterators, bulk import, schema evolution, aliases for zero-downtime reindexing, milvus.yaml configuration, LangChain integration and Zilliz Cloud, ending with a hybrid product search capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Milvus beginner level or can create schemas, insert data, build AUTOINDEX and run filtered searches with MilvusClient
Can compute recall@k against brute-force ground truth with NumPy
Has a running Milvus Standalone instance via Docker Compose with at least 16 GB RAM and a 1-million-vector public dataset available
outcomes: Tune HNSW, IVF and quantized indexes in Milvus against measured recall, latency and memory targets
Design multi-tenant collections with partition keys, scalar indexes and an appropriate consistency level
Build full-text and hybrid dense plus sparse search with BM25 functions, analyzers and rerankers
Run production data workflows: bulk import, schema evolution, alias-based reindexing and Zilliz Cloud deployment

advanced.summary: For platform, SRE and senior backend engineers who run Milvus in production or are about to. Covers the Milvus 2.6 architecture (proxy, coordinator, streaming, query and data nodes, etcd, object storage and the WAL), segment lifecycle and compaction, Kubernetes deployment with the Milvus Operator and Helm, message queue choices, DiskANN, mmap and GPU indexes, replicas and resource groups, clustering compaction, RBAC and security hardening, milvus-backup, Prometheus and Grafana monitoring, quotas, function-based embedding and reranking, benchmarking, upgrades, troubleshooting, Zilliz Cloud migration and CDC, ending with a production cluster capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Milvus intermediate level or tunes indexes, partition keys, hybrid search and consistency levels in Milvus already
Operates Kubernetes with kubectl and Helm, including StatefulSets, PersistentVolumes and namespaces
Has a Kubernetes cluster with at least 3 worker nodes of 16 GB RAM (kind or k3d acceptable for most labs), an S3-compatible bucket and optional NVIDIA GPU node
outcomes: Explain the Milvus data path from proxy to WAL to segments in object storage and use it to diagnose latency and freshness problems
Deploy, scale and upgrade Milvus Distributed on Kubernetes with the Milvus Operator or Helm
Secure, back up, monitor and rate-limit a production Milvus cluster with RBAC, TLS, milvus-backup, Prometheus and Grafana
Select disk, memory-mapped and GPU index strategies and validate them with VectorDBBench against SLOs
